catalog_quote: All Kiwaian languages have relatively simple phonologies which are very similar in most of them. ... The suprasegmental systems are relatively complicated and manifest themselves in complex stress systems with rhythm patterns, and a two-tone system is present in all the languages, except apparently in Wabuda. Its functional load appears to be low in all the languages except for North-Eastern Kiwai and (Arigibi ?) where it seems to be quite high. The syllable structures are very simple; no consonant clusters occur (except for the very rare presence of -nd- in Kerewo) and all syllables are open.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for stress placement is given. Wurm states, for every Kiwaian language including Morigi, that word prosody consists of a 'complex' stress system organised in rhythm patterns together with a two-tone system whose functional load is low (in Morigi, i.e. everywhere except NE Kiwai/Arigibi). The only Morigi-specific stress datum found anywhere is one word with a penultimate stress mark in Wurm 1951 (Tu. buhére), seen only as a Google Books snippet.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed (the 'rhythm patterns' remark implies alternating prominence but nothing is specified).
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress; tone reported absent 'apparently' in Wabuda and of high functional load only in North-Eastern Kiwai and (Arigibi ?).
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level statement covering 'all Kiwaian languages'; not a Morigi-specific description and no word-vs-phrase domain is stated. Wurm 1973 p.250 adds that 'Stress features [are] yet to be studied in detail in North-Eastern Kiwai and the other Kiwaian languages'.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement is family-level ('all Kiwaian languages'), not a Morigi-specific description. Older sources call the language 'Turama' (Ray 1923; Wurm 1951 abbrev. 'Tu.'), and Capell 1962 / Franklin 1968 refer to 'Morigi Island' or 'Wariadai'. Wurm 1973 treats Morigi as a communalect very closely related to Kerewo (kere1263) that may ultimately be a dialect of a single Turama-Kerewo language; Wurm 1971 treats Morigi as one of two dialects of Turama-Kerewo (Goari). No source describes a Morigi stress rule.
